title: Introduce gradual reserve unifier and per-pool utilization heartbeat
author: Sofia Ramos
body:
Motivation: In high-churn tenant fleets we observed many small, short-lived reservations that fragment pool capacity and inflate headroom estimates. This leads to unstable autoscaler decisions (frequent scale ups followed by rapid scale downs) and noisy utilization metrics. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) a Gradual Reserve Unifier controller that periodically coalesces adjacent or rapidly renewing micro-reservations into a single logical reservation to reduce fragmentation and smooth headroom; and (2) a lightweight per-pool Utilization Heartbeat emitter that samples and reports reservoir-level utilization percentile snapshots at a configurable cadence. The goal is to improve autoscaler stability and give SREs more reliable percentile-based signals for throughput guarantees.

What this changes (summary):
- controller/gradual_unifier.go: new controller that scans pool reservations and merges candidates according to time-window and affinity rules. It exposes config knobs: unify_window_ms, min_reservation_age_ms, max_merge_factor.
- telemetry/pool_heartbeat.go: new emitter that publishes a small telemetry event (utilization_p50/p90/p99, active_reservations, reserved_capacity) every heartbeat. Events are routed to the existing telemetry pipeline with a new metric namespace dedicated.pool_heartbeat.
- config/defaults.yaml: defaults for the unifier and heartbeat (disabled in Private by default; can be enabled via dedicated.features.unifier=true).
- charts/dedicated/values.yaml: Helm flags for operators to opt-in and tune parameters per deployment class.
- docs/ops/gradual-reserve-unifier.md: operational runbook, rollout steps, observability dashboard examples and rollback guidance.
- tests/unifier_e2e.go: synthetic e2e harness that exercises fragmentation and verifies autoscaler stability improvements (asserts decrease in scale-flap frequency).

Design notes: The unifier only touches reservations with compatible affinity labels and only merges when merge factor results in >=10% reduction in active reservations for the same capacity footprint (configurable). We intentionally avoid global locking: merges are append-only transforms that create a new unified reservation and mark old reservations for graceful expiry to prevent mid-flight eviction of tailing requests. The heartbeat emitter samples internal ringbuffers rather than full KV scans to keep overhead under 0.2% CPU for large pools.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated off by default in cloud-hosted; enable in internal canary clusters for 48h.
2) Run telemetry-only (heartbeat enabled, unifier disabled) for 72h to validate metric signal stability.
3) Enable unifier in a single low-traffic pool with conservative params (unify_window_ms=30000, max_merge_factor=4).
4) Gradually increase rollout if scaling flaps reduce and service-level throughput remains within 0.5% of baseline.

Benchmarks and results: Local perf lab simulated 50k reservations with median lifetime 12s. With unifier+heartbeat enabled we saw: 45% drop in reservation count variance, tail autoscale events reduced by ~60%, controller CPU overhead +0.15% at 99th percentile. E2E harness shows median request latency unchanged; 95th percentile improved by ~3% under high churn.

Security and config: No secret material. Operators can opt out. The unifier respects tenant isolation labels and cannot merge reservations across tenant boundaries (enforced in code and tested).

Related work: builds on ENG-1678 (reservation lifecycle rewrite) and complements ENG-7692 (stabilized-autoscaler). See SUP-3421 for customer-reported fragmentation incident that motivated the work.

Notes for reviewers: key safety checks are in tests/unifier_e2e.go and unit tests around affinity matching. Pay attention to edge cases around reservation expiry races; I added a small jitter to the expiry window to avoid thundering merges.

review_comments:
Maya Ivanov: This looks promising — please double-check tenant isolation and race windows; the merge path must be idempotent.

S. Ramos (author): Answered: unifier marks old reservations as 'deprecated' and we expire them via the normal lifecycle; added tests to cover idempotency.

Ravi Singh: CI e2e flaked once under high concurrency — can you add a retry to the harness and make failure deterministic?

S. Ramos: Added retry + tightened timing in tests; CI rerun passed.

Elena Gomez: Request: add a dashboard tile showing 'merged_reservations/sec' and a rollback playbook.

S. Ramos: Added dashboard snippet to docs and an operator rollback section (docs/ops/gradual-reserve-unifier.md).

Maya Ivanov: Approved after address comments.

Automated CI: initial unit tests pass, integration tests failed on first run (timeout), integration re-run pass, e2e passed in synthetic harness. Linter: pass. Security scan: no findings.
notes: Operator-configurable and opt-in for Private installs; recommended canary first. Observability additions are lightweight and routed to existing pipeline. The intent is to reduce scale-flapping driven by reservation churn without changing admission semantics.
release_notes: Add optional 'Gradual Reserve Unifier' to coalesce short-lived reservations and a low-overhead 'per-pool utilization heartbeat' metric to improve autoscaler stability and utilization visibility. Feature is disabled by default and must be enabled by operators in dedicated.features.unifier. Rollout guidance provided in docs/ops/gradual-reserve-unifier.md.
impact_assessment: Latency: no client-visible changes expected. Cost: minor controller CPU +0.1-0.3% in large pools. Risk: medium-low; potential for unexpected reservation consolidation if misconfigured; safeguards included (tenant boundaries, affinity checks, opt-out).
changelog_entry: features: introduce gradual reserve unifier + dedicated.pool_heartbeat telemetry.
